RaceOS

What if racing data could suggest when to make a pit stop?

Where it stands
Completed learning prototype, not a validated strategy engine for real F1 races.

A closer look

Explore the live build ↗Source code ↗The working RaceOS experience is available through the linked Streamlit app.

THE SPARK

Why this one?

Formula 1 strategy depends on timing and judgment. RaceOS was an experiment in whether a small machine-learning system could learn some of those decisions from race data.

THE BUILD

How it works

A Streamlit interface that accepts race conditions such as driver, lap, compound, tyre life and position, then uses a Random Forest model and rule-based scoring to produce an experimental pit-stop recommendation.

Python · Streamlit · Pandas · scikit-learn

THE COMPONENTS

Inside the project

  • Interactive race-condition inputs
  • Model recommendation and probability
  • Risk and strategy guidance

CURRENT CHAPTER

Progress & evidence

A public Streamlit app and a repository with training and prediction code are linked.

Completed learning prototype, not a validated strategy engine for real F1 races.
